Edition 2024 puts Future in the prelude, so the absence of an import is correct, not an oversight. The dyn-incompatibility cost is recorded as a NEGATIVE consequence in adr-0002, with the A-2 wrapper-trait escape hatch spelled out, rather than hidden.

The gap analyze could not verify by grep is closed by reading: both matches in exhaustividad_resultado_envio.rs (reaccion_del_nucleo lines 46-52, etapa_del_acuse lines 60-65) enumerate every variant with no `_` arm and no `..` rest pattern, and ResultadoEnvio carries no #[non_exhaustive].

The four bite experiments in cotejo section 5 are credible under arithmetic checking: every quoted line:col resolves against the real files. E0004 at exhaustividad:46:11 is the match scrutinee; E0599 at 27:21 is the variant path inside the const array, and LimiteDeTasa really does appear in exactly three places, matching 'due to 3 previous errors'; E0063 at guardian:135:18 is the EventoEntrante initializer; the 5.4 panics at 120:13 and 148:9 are the two assert! macro sites, and 'test result: FAILED. 2 passed; 2 failed' matches the four tests in that file, of which exactly the last two inspect content.

131047 arbitration judged on the merits against the official Cloud API error-code page, not merely against the blueprint: 131047 ('More than 24 hours have passed since the recipient last replied to the sender number') is the only published closed-window code and no separate template-required code exists, so the inverse assignment would leave FueraDeVentana with no official anchor at all. The blueprint choice is therefore the better of the two readings, and cotejo section 2 states both paths without ambiguity: round trip answered 131047 produces FueraDeVentana, pre-flight window-closed plus RespuestaLibre produces PlantillaRequerida.

Residual for A-2, not a blocker: one world state (window closed plus RespuestaLibre) can surface as either variant depending on whether the adapter holds fresh window state, so a cold start or a stale cache yields FueraDeVentana where a warm adapter yields PlantillaRequerida. The cotejo describes both paths but never states that the core must treat them as equivalent. The A-2 contract-test battery against the simulated adapter should pin that equivalence.

The guardian binds the test-local TablaDeMapeo stand-in, not production code, because no adapter exists yet; experiment 5.4 therefore mutates the fixture it verifies. This is declared honestly in the guardian header and in cotejo section 6 (lexical check necessary but insufficient; this cotejo certifies form and documentary anchoring, not behavior), and the assertions have to be re-pointed at the real adapter in A-3. Experiment 5.4 does establish the property the parent asked about: an identity-function mapping passes the lexical check and still fails two guardian assertions at run time.

Newtypes IdRemitente and IdDeduplicacion beyond the single IdConversacion the blueprint named are justified in adr-0002 decision 7 and forced by EventoEntrante; the alternative, a raw String, is precisely the transport leak adr-0010 forbids. Opacity is genuine at the type level (private tuple field, three mutually incompatible types), but the public nuevo()/como_str() pair means opacity against deliberate misuse rests on the guardian and on review rather than on the type system, which identidad.rs states openly instead of overclaiming.

DURACION_VENTANA_SERVICIO is a public item beyond the seven enumerated FR-12 elements, but FR-12 element 4 names the 24-hour window normatively, so it sits inside the declared vocabulary of the port rather than being Cloud API policy leaking into the domain. It is unused and correctly documented as never produced on the own channel.

FAKE-GREEN FLAG against 05-validation.json, not against the diff: the output_excerpt values for the four cargo commands are paraphrased rather than captured. Entry 1 claims 'Finished release [optimized] target(s)' for `cargo build --workspace`, which actually prints 'Finished `dev` profile [unoptimized + debuginfo] target(s)'; entry 3 claims 'Checked formatting' for `cargo fmt --check`, which prints nothing at all on success; entry 4 claims 'Finished release' for clippy. The commands themselves genuinely pass, so this is an artifact-integrity defect and not a false pass, but an excerpt asserting a release profile for a debug build is exactly the pattern review exists to catch.
